_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.usage_guidance: Confirms PiliApp genuinely localized to Finnish (unlike its sl/et/lv/lt subdomains, which 302-redirect to English) — a real, established competitor UI term.

phrases.english_concept: colloquial one-word term for the letters ä, ö (and å) — the characters at risk from decorative Unicode
phrases.register: informal but universally understood; standard in Finnish tech/forum writing
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'skandit' in FAQ headings and body copy on any fi page that explains what happens to ä/ö in a styled name. The natural search formulations are built around it: 'skandit ei näy', 'skandit hajoaa', 'skandiongelma'. Note the colloquial verb agreement — Finns write 'skandit ei näy' (singular verb) in forum register even though the written standard is 'skandit eivät näy'; a page can use the standard form in headings and the colloquial one nowhere, but should be aware searchers type the colloquial one.
phrases.good_example: Miksi skandit eivät näy, kun kopioin tyylitellyn nimen?
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'skandit' in formal/legal/accessibility copy — there use 'skandinaaviset merkit' or name the letters. Do not use it in an H1 as the primary target; it is problem vocabulary, not demand vocabulary.

phrases.english_concept: the letters ä and ö specifically (second colloquial term)
phrases.register: informal-neutral, widely used including in tech documentation
phrases.usage_guidance: Interchangeable with 'skandit' in most FAQ contexts; prefer 'ääkköset' when the sentence is specifically about ä and ö in text/typing, and 'skandit' when it is about character-encoding failure. Do not use both in the same heading as if they were different concepts.
phrases.good_example: Useimmissa tyyleissä ei ole ääkkösiä, joten ä ja ö muuttuvat tavallisiksi kirjaimiksi.
phrases.avoid_when: Not for formal/legal copy. Do not use it to refer to å (that is 'ruotsalainen o' or covered by 'skandit').

phrases.english_concept: the searched form of a phrase is case-inflected, not the dictionary form (structural finding)
phrases.usage_guidance: In an fi page title use the hyphenated compound ('Instagram-fontit'); in instruction and FAQ sentences use the illative ('kopioi ja liitä Instagramiin', 'fontit Instagramiin'). The same pattern applies to every platform: 'TikTokiin', 'Discordiin', 'bioon', 'profiiliin'. Getting the case endings right on borrowed platform names is one of the clearest hand-written-vs-machine-translated signals available in Finnish.
phrases.good_example: Valitse tyyli, kopioi teksti ja liitä se Instagramiin tai TikTokiin.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not write the unhyphenated 'Instagram fontit' anywhere. Do not force the illative into a title where the compound is more natural.

phrases.english_concept: font (which Finnish word people actually type)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'fontti' throughout. Mention 'kirjasin' at most once, in an FAQ, if disambiguation genuinely helps. 'Tekstigeneraattori' (FI-001) remains the tool head term; 'fontti' is the object word.
phrases.good_example: Valitse fontti ja kopioi teksti — se toimii sellaisenaan Instagramissa.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'kirjasin' in headings or UI labels — it reads as either archaic or as a specialist typography term, and it also means 'printing type'.

phrases.english_concept: bold (style name) — and the machine-translation trap around it
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'lihavoitu teksti' as the style name and 'lihavointi' when referring to the formatting action. The site already uses this correctly at fi/lihavoitu-teksti — the value of this record is documenting the trap so it is never 'corrected' toward the competitor's wording.
phrases.good_example: Lihavoitu teksti sosiaaliseen mediaan — kopioi ja liitä.
phrases.avoid_when: Never use 'rohkea' for bold in any context on this site.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'kaunokirjoitus' for the cursive/script style and for cursive practice-sheet copy; keep 'kursivoitu' strictly for italic. The site already has fi/kursivoitu-teksti — confirm that page is genuinely about italic, and if it is meant to serve cursive demand, that is a naming problem to raise, not to silently fix.
phrases.good_example: Kirjoita nimesi kaunokirjoituksella ja kopioi se bioon.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'kaunokirjoitus' to label the italic style; do not split the compound.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'nimimerkki' as the neutral term and 'nikki' only in explicitly gaming-register sections. Keep 'käyttäjätunnus' for the login field and 'profiilinimi' for the displayed name — the same three-way split as sv/da. FAQ headings should use the inflected forms Finns actually type ('Miten keksin hyvän nimimerkin?').
phrases.good_example: En keksi hyvää nimimerkkiä — kokeile tyylittelyä ja koristemerkkejä.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'nikki' outside gaming/youth contexts. Do not use 'nimimerkki' for a real-name display field, and do not use 'lempinimi' (an affectionate real-life nickname) for a gaming handle.

phrases.english_concept: special characters / symbols to copy (and the case form searched)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use the nominative plural 'erikoismerkit' in an H1 that names the collection, and the partitive 'erikoismerkkejä' in body sentences about copying/getting them. Do not use the singular citation form as a heading. Same pattern governs 'koristemerkit'/'koristemerkkejä' for decorative symbols and 'symbolit'/'symboleja'.
phrases.good_example: Erikoismerkit — kopioi symboleja suoraan nimeesi tai bioosi.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'erikoismerkki' (singular) as a page heading. Do not use 'erikoismerkit' to refer to ä/ö — those are ordinary Finnish letters, and calling them special characters is exactly the framing error a Finnish reader will notice (see P16/P17).

phrases.register: neutral; spans nostalgic/educational and font-shopping contexts
phrases.usage_guidance: Do not lead a page's title/H1 with this term without a dedicated Semrush/GSC SERP pull first -- the dominant open-web sense is nostalgic/educational, not transactional, so a title built on the naive 'fancy letters' reading risks mismatching most of the term's real search intent. Safe as a secondary FAQ/body mention tied to decorative/cursive-style fonts specifically, with framing that disambiguates rather than assuming the word alone signals transactional intent.
phrases.good_example: Kaunokirjaimet-tyylinen, käsinkirjoitettua muistuttava fontti sopii kutsukortteihin ja tatuointeihin.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as a page's primary title/H1 term without confirming real SERP composition first (Semrush was out of API units in both this pass and the prior RUN-025 pass, so this has never been verified against actual ranking pages). Do not conflate with 'tekstauskirjaimet'/'tikkukirjaimet' (print/block capitals) -- confirmed a different, unrelated word family.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use for headings, logos, greeting/invitation cards, posters, and short high-impact text (e.g. an Instagram bio) -- every native source found frames decorative fonts this way. Do not imply suitability for long-form/body text.
phrases.avoid_when: Never claim koristeellinen fonts are good for long/body text -- every native source found says the opposite (readability risk).

phrases.usage_guidance: Usable in tattoo/lettering-style copy as a natural, real shorthand for cursive/script style -- pairs naturally with 'kaunokirjoitus' (the fuller form) rather than replacing it everywhere.
phrases.avoid_when: Register-specific to informal/tattoo-community writing -- do not use as a formal/professional-register synonym for kaunokirjoitus.

phrases.english_concept: pejorative for cluttered leetspeak/decorative gaming names
phrases.usage_guidance: This is NOT copy to use on-page -- it's a design constraint for the gamename/flair engine's Finnish-facing framing. Presenting decorative Unicode flair as an earnest 'epic gamer' xX...Xx aesthetic risks landing as exactly the cliché Finnish gamers have spent over a decade mocking. Lean toward flair framed as deliberate/stylish/ironic rather than naive 'coolness', or toward game-appropriate theming rather than generic leetspeak clutter.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in user-facing copy -- this is a negative/mocking term, captured for its strategic implication, not for use as vocabulary.

phrases.english_concept: Discord handle terminology (current, post-2023 username system)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'käyttäjätunnus'/'tunnus' specifically when discussing Discord's current unique-handle system; keep 'nimimerkki' for the older display-name concept or other platforms.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'nimimerkki' and 'käyttäjätunnus' interchangeably for Discord specifically -- they now name two different, sequential systems.

phrases.english_concept: italic (formal meaning) vs. real lay conflation with cursive/joined script
phrases.register: formal sense = print/technical; conflated sense = lay/everyday
phrases.usage_guidance: If a page offers both an italic style AND a cursive/joined-script style, consider explicit FAQ disambiguation ('kursivoitu tarkoittaa kallistettua tekstiä; jos etsit yhdistettyä käsialatyyliä, se on kaunokirjoitusta') rather than assuming the search term alone signals which style the user wants.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not silently equate 'kursivoitu' with cursive-script styling in copy aimed at a design-literate audience (professional register keeps them distinct) -- the ambiguity is a lay-register phenomenon.

phrases.english_concept: font generator (primary head term, market leader phrasing)
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary title/H1 head term, used by the market-leading competitor.
